children: Stocks in Indonesian coal miner PT Bayan Resources
jumped as much as 20% on Friday after the company announced a deal to sell 10 billion shares to tycoon Andi Syamsuddin Arsyad, who is also known as Haji Isam.
The price rose to 13,825 rupiah ($0.7793) per share on Friday, its highest level in over a week.
Bayan said its biggest shareholders, Low Tuck Kwong and Elaine Low, signed a conditional agreement to sell 10 billion shares to PT Jhonlin Baratama, a company controlled by Haji Isam.
Upon completion of the deal, PT Jhonlin Baratama will hold a stake of around 30% in Bayan.

Low Tuck Kwong currently holds 13 billion shares in the company with Elaine Low holding 7 billion. Together, they now control around 62% of Bayan Resources, valued at around $13 billion, according to LSEG Refinitiv data.
Bayan did not disclose the potential value of the deal for the 10-billion-share sale.
Bayan and three of its subsidiaries declared force majeure on their coal supply obligations on Monday, saying that their 2026 mining quotas had not yet been increased.
